comment.narrative: Between January and March 2022, HALO Ukraine took part in 8 capacity development and stakeholder meetings, this included:•Three UNDP-coordinated Mine Action SubCluster meetings (two general subcluster meetings and one meeting regarding the UN Flash Appeal)•One Information Management Working Group Meeting•One EORE Working Group Meeting•One HALO organised meeting with DRC and FSD colleagues to coordinate on EORE messaging•One UN Protection Cluster Meeting•One GICHD led coordination meeting on capacity development effortsHALO also participated in a large number of coordination meetings regarding the humanitarian response for the Ukraine crisis.

Between October and December 2022, HALO took part in:• UN HRP Planning Workshop• HMA Working Group • Three UNDP-coordinated Mine Action SubCluster meetings• One EORE Working Group Meeting• One meeting with the MOD representatives• Two meetings with the SESIn November, 2022 HALO had a meeting with the Dutch Ambassador in Ukraine. HALO provided an update on its current operations and expansion plans, and discussed HALO coordination work with the governmental stakeholders, as well as advocacy matters.

During the 1st quarter of 2023 HALO attended a range of meetings with the government and other humanitarian stakeholders, including but not limited to: - US Embassy;- Norway; - Swiss Embassy;- Canada MFA;- State Emergency Service;- Ministry of Reintegration of the Temporarily Occupied Territories;- EUAM;- UNDP;- GIZ;HALO will continue active engagement with partners over the course of 2023.

During the 2-nd quarter of 2023 HALO attended a range of meetings with the government and other humanitarian stakeholders, including but not limited to: British Embassy; MASC; Swiss MFA; Finnish MFA; REACH Ukraine; Dutch MFA; Norwegian MFA; Merefa SESU; IOM; Prometheus. HALO will continue active engagement with partners over the course of 2023.

During the 3-d quarter of 2023 HALO attended a range of meetings with the government and other humanitarian stakeholders, including but not limited to:Mykolaiv Mine Action Operators; DG ECHO; VEA Systems; Demine Ukraine Forum

HALO participated in 6 meetings attended by representatives from the Ukrainian Ministry of Defence (MOD), State Emergency Service (SES), OSCE Project Co-ordinator in Ukraine (PCU), and other international mine action operators. This included Mine Action Sub-Cluster meetings to discuss legislative developments and provide recommendations, and meetings to coordinate NTS and EORE activities and thereby to avoid a duplication of work.

HALO participated in 6 mine action stakeholder meetings in the quarter. This included a two-day roundtable event in Sievierodonetsk in March regarding operational plans for 2021 and implementation of the amendment to the Mine Action Law passed in December 2020. The event was organised by the OSCU PCU and attended by government stakeholders from the MOD and SES; the Ambassadors of Sweden, Slovakia, Norway and Croatia; the OSCE PCU ambassador; and GICHD representatives. HALO also attended the first mine action information management working group for Ukraine oganised by GICHD, three monthly mine action Sub-Cluster meetings, and a UN OCHA General Coordination meeting for Ukraine.In addition, HALO Ukraine representatives also attended a visit to a new currently non-functioning civilian crossing point across the ‘contact line’ at Shchastya, Luhansk region by a delegation including President of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelenskyi, and President of the European Council, Charles Michel in March 2021.

HALO took part in 12 capacity development meetings and events:• Three UNDP-coordinated Mine Action Subcluster meetings• Four meetings of the GICHD-led Information Management Working Group• One update meeting regarding the information management system for mine action’s setup (IMSMA) in Ukraine• Two meetings of the NMAS Working Group• One OSCE-PCU organised biannual roundtable for Mine Action sector planning• One DRC-UNDP workshop on coordination of EORE and victim assistance in mine action in Ukraine

In this quarter, HALO took part in 10 stakeholder meetings and events: • Two UNDP-coordinated Mine Action Subcluster meetings, • Four meetings of the GICHD-led Information Management Working Group, • One meeting of the NMAS Working Group, • One UN Protection Cluster Contingency Planning workshop• One UN General Coordination meeting • And HALO also hosted a joint visit to Stepove, Luhansk region for the OSCE SMM Mine Action Unit and the UN Mine Action SubCluster Co-ordinator.

In this quarter, HALO took part in 11 events:• Two UNDP-coordinated Mine Action Subcluster meetings• Two meetings of the GICHD-led Information Management Working Group• One Mine Victim Assistance Working Group• One Follow up with UNDP/DRC on Mine victim assistance working group meeting• One UNDP Gender mainstreaming in Mine Action event• One meeting with mine action stakeholders at the Merefa SES Humanitarian Demining Centre• One meeting with mine action stakeholders at the Chernihiv MOD Mine Action Centre• One meeting and a separate event with the Ministry of TOT Reintegration regarding their future activities in the mine action sphere.

In this quarter, HALO took part in:• Five UNDP-coordinated Mine Action SubCluster meetings• One Information Management working group meeting• One EORE working group meeting• 2 GICHD-led meetings on IMSMA and EORE • 3 meetings with the national stakeholers (Mine Action department of the Ministry of Defence, SES in Brovary and Chernihiv oblast)Moreover, in this reporting period, James Cowan CEO of The HALO Trust visited Ukraine and met with the Ukrainian Ministry of Defence, Ukrainian Army and State Emergency Service representatives. The CEO also had the meetings the Head of OCHA, and Mine Action Subcluster coordinator.In addition, HALO conducted an initial visit to Chernihiv region in this quarter in preparation for expanding its operations to the region. HALO also participated in a series of coordination meetings with NGOs working in Ukraine.

Within the reporting period HALO participated in:• Five UNDP-coordinated Mine Action SubCluster meetings• Two coordination meetings with SES• A coordination meeting with UNICEFIn addition, HALO also undertook a recce to Sumy region in August to meet with a range of key national stakeholders in the region. HALO also met with other non-mine action NGOs to establish areas for coordination and partnership between our activities.

comment.narrative: Rising COVID-19 cases in eastern Ukraine in the quarter postponed EORE sessions taking place under this project.

The COVID-19 situation has severely limited the Dutch-funded NTS team’s opportunities to conduct EORE. Their EORE activities were planned to complement their NTS work and take place alongside in similar locations. However, thus far, their NTS work has focused on areas in or near the buffer zone, where the need is greatest but where there is also a disproportionately high number of elderly and disabled people, who are particularly vulnerable to infection. Consequently, given high rates of COVID-19 in Ukraine, gathering groups of such vulnerable people together for sessions or even going door-to-door has been considered unnecessarily risky. In addition, in this quarter schools were largely closed for the summer holidays and access to summer camps was limited for external visitors due to COVID-19 precautions.HALO Ukraine has requested permission to focus the cross-trained team's work on survey activities throughout the rest of the grant and move away from EORE. The aim is to complete a full baseline survey of mine/ERW contamination in Ukrainian Government controlled areas of Donetsk and Luhansk regions.
The cross trained team undertook refresher EORE training this quarter. It is planned that EORE sessions will start, COVID-19 permitting, in the next quarter.

comment.narrative: Clearance activities took place across eight clearance tasks in Donetsk region and 12 clearance tasks in Luhansk region this quarter. Spring weather condition enabled solid progress.

Clearance activities took place on five clearance sites in Donetsk region. Similarly to the previous quarter, teams worked in two areas with mixed threat types requiring surface tripwire clearance and then sub-surface anti-vehicle mine clearance. Clearance teams were able to restart activities in the last week of January following the annual winter stand down.
Clearance activities took place on four clearance tasks in Donetsk region and eight clearance tasks in Luhansk region this quarter. Productivity remained strong.

Clearance activities took place on two clearance tasks in Donetsk region and five clearance tasks in Luhansk region this quarter. Due to the winter conditions and the annual winter stand-down, productivity was lower than in the previous reporting period.

Clearance teams worked on seven clearance sites in Donetsk region. They worked on two mixed-threat minefields that required two-stage clearance to search for items laid with tripwire on the surface as well as sub-surface anti-vehicle mines. 40% of land cleared was in areas where remotely controlled vegetation cutters, known as Robocuts, removed vegetation first, which significantly sped up the search for tripwires. The teams were stood down on their annual winter stand-down in late December as sub-zero temperatures made manual clearance impractical or impossible.

comment.narrative: 17 areas where Dutch clearance teams had worked on under this project were handed over to local communities. 13 of these underwent external quality control visits in the previous quarter, and four more underwent external quality control in October.

HALO has noticed an inconsistency in reporting land returned to the community for Q4 2022 - the amount of land returned equals a sum of land released, reduced and cancelled. This number has been corrected in the version of the metrics for Q1 2023.

In September, two tasks that Dutch teams had worked on under this project were handed back to local communities following external quality control visits. In addition, external quality control was conducted by the MOD's Demining Centre for 13 further areas where Dutch-funded teams have worked under this grant, where clearance has been completed. The COVID-19 situation permitting, these areas will be handed over to communities in the coming months.

Quality control (QC) visits from representatives of the MoD's National Mine Action Authority are planned for July and August 2021, on completion of QC, cleared areas can be handed over to communities.

comment.narrative: Rising COVID-19 cases in eastern Ukraine in the quarter postponed EORE sessions taking place under this project.

The COVID-19 situation has severely limited the Dutch-funded NTS team�s opportunities to conduct EORE. Their EORE activities were planned to complement their NTS work and take place alongside in similar locations. However, thus far, their NTS work has focused on areas in or near the buffer zone, where the need is greatest but where there is also a disproportionately high number of elderly and disabled people, who are particularly vulnerable to infection. Consequently, given high rates of COVID-19 in Ukraine, gathering groups of such vulnerable people together for sessions or even going door-to-door has been considered unnecessarily risky. In addition, in this quarter schools were largely closed for the summer holidays and access to summer camps was limited for external visitors due to COVID-19 precautions.HALO Ukraine has requested permission to focus the cross-trained team's work on survey activities throughout the rest of the grant and move away from EORE. The aim is to complete a full baseline survey of mine/ERW contamination in Ukrainian Government controlled areas of Donetsk and Luhansk regions.
The cross trained team undertook refresher EORE training this quarter. It is planned that EORE sessions will start, COVID-19 permitting, in the next quarter.

comment.narrative: Advocacy and planning activities took place in this quarter, however, it was not possible to undertake operational activities. Redeployment of clearance and survey teams, following the winter standdown, was planned to resume in late January/early February depending on the weather. However, very high rates of COVID-19 in early February were not conducive to gathering groups of people for in-person refresher training and the security situation remained tense and at risk of escalation. The deteriorating security situation further deteriorated until thestart of start of the Russian multi-axis offensive on Ukrainian territory on 24 February 2022, making it impossible to redeploy teams and conduct activities as per the project plan. At the time of writing (1 May 2022), HALO is about to start operational redeployment in new locations in Ukraine.

HALO deployed Dutch-funded manual teams across four tasks in Kyiv region in the reporting quarter. The Programme has now operational presence in Kyiv, Chernihiv, Sumy regions. In addition, the survey teams started working in Kharkiv oblast in early November.

In April, seeing that Russian forces were retreating from northern Ukraine, which fundamentally changed the security situation in those areas, as well as noting the deteriorating security situation in eastern Ukraine HALO continued to advise staff members to leave Donbas. HALO set up a logistics base in Vinnytsia and started to liaise with relevant authorities to start humanitarian mine action operations in Kyiv region, receiving permission to conduct NTS and clearance in Kyiv region from 1 May. Then, phased refresher trainings were conducted for existing non-technical and clearance teams, followed by deployment of the teams Kyiv. HALO chose to locate its main new operating base in Brovary; more than 200 of our staff from Donbas have moved with HALO to the new area of operations. Towards the end of June, HALO also received permission from the Ukrainian Ministry of Defence to undertake non-technical survey and clearance operations in Chernihiv region also. Given the huge need and the geographical scope of the work, HALO started external recruitment and trainings to expand to meet these challenges. To help ensure the sustainability of the project, HALO applied for and received temporary conscription exemptions for over 130 trained staff members; we will continue to apply for further exemptions. The phased nature of the redeployment means that no Dutch teams were deployed in this quarter. Dutch-funding has been vital to supporting HALO and its staff through these changes. Dutch-funded teams will be deployed in the next quarter.

Within the reporting period two Dutch-funded manual teams worked across three tasks located in Kyiv region until mid-December. All clearance operations were then suspended for winter stand down due to harsh winter conditions. The Programme will recommence phased deployment of manual and mechanical clearance teams around March 2023, as soon as the weather allows.

comment.narrative: Clearance activities took place across eight clearance tasks in Donetsk region and 12 clearance tasks in Luhansk region this quarter. Spring weather condition enabled solid progress.

Clearance activities took place on five clearance sites in Donetsk region.
